description: USAGE FLOAT-LONG (implementor-defined double-precision float, mapped to native double). LIVE (P12 step 2): compiles at 2002+, COBOL0900 below. Representation implementor-defined per §2023:13.18.60.4 GR13/GR21. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 USAGE clause's general format (§1985:VI.5.14.2) is `[ USAGE IS ] { BINARY | COMPUTATIONAL | COMP | DISPLAY | INDEX | PACKED-DECIMAL }` and nothing else, its §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR3 naming the numeric usages it has: 'a USAGE clause specifying BINARY, COMPUTATIONAL, or PACKED-DECIMAL must be declared with a PICTURE character-string that describes a numeric item'; §2002:13.16.58.3 GR12 has the trio: 'The usages float-short, float-long and float-extended define signed numeric data items that are held in a floating-point format suitable for the machine on which the runtime module is to run', §2002:13.16.58.3 GR13 makes their 'representation and length' implementor-defined, §2002:F.1 item 6 lists FLOAT-SHORT, FLOAT-LONG and FLOAT-EXTENDED among 'The following reserved words have been added', and §2002:F.2 item 7 states the change: 'The floating-point type exists both in a numeric form, with a machine-specific representation, and in a numeric-edited form.' §2014:13.18.60.3 GR12 and GR20 carry the 2002 rules unchanged, so 2014 = 2023 (the ISO-60559-pinned FLOAT-BINARY-*/FLOAT-DECIMAL-* family is a separate 2014 row).
